All 46 tests pass (43 existing + TC-125, TC-126, TC-127), and the build succeeds.

## Report

**Files modified** (within allowed scope):
- `source-fe/src/api/customerApi.js` — `listCustomers` now takes `{ status, ...options }`, builds `/customers?status=<encoded>` when `status` is truthy, else plain `/customers`; `status` is destructured out before `request()` so it never leaks into `fetch` init.
- `source-fe/test/customerApi.test.js` — added TC-125, TC-126, TC-127 as a contiguous block after TC-102.

**Tests added:**
- `TC-125: listCustomers sends one GET whose URL carries the status filter` — 7 rows (`{}`, `''`, `undefined`, `null`, `'ACTIVE'`, `'INACTIVE'`, `'A&B=C D'`), checks URL and that `init` is exactly `{ headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } }`.
- `TC-126: listCustomers returns the array sent by the API without filtering or sorting` — 4 rows including mismatched status, out-of-id-order, and empty arrays.
- `TC-127: listCustomers throws ApiError with the status and field errors of the API` — 400 and 500 cases, checks `error.status`, `error.fieldErrors`, and that exactly one request with the right URL was sent.

**Test results:** `fe_build` and `fe_test` both pass — 46/46 tests green, no existing test touched (the pre-existing `listCustomers calls GET /api/customers and returns the body` test still passes unmodified, confirming backward compatibility).

No design questions arose; implementation follows D6 and the plan's T4 spec exactly.
